To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carbonization of a polymer of intrinsic micporosity to a microporous carbon results in the retention of the microporosity and of nitrogen functionalities that are responsible for time- and pH-dependent capacitance switching.
a polymer of intrinsic micporosity (PIM) can be directly carbonized into a microporus carbon (heterocarbon) that is capable of switching its capacitance in aqueous electrolytes over a wide pH-range.

a microporous carbon material with nitrogen functionalities in the polymer structure is obtained by vacuum carbonization of PIM-EA-TBT at 700 ° C and exhibits unusual time-, electrolyt-, and pH dependent properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of a microporous carbon material that is derived from a nitrogen-containing polymer of high intrinsic microporocity.
the development of a new class of materials with high surface areas and unusual properties.

the development of a new family of carbon materials that combine high specific surface areas and nitrogen functionalities and are thus promising for applications in energy and environmental technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heterocarbon is not a “true” pseudocapacitor material but a “true” capacitor material.
the carbonized PIMs are not just a new type of carbon but a new class of materials.
the microporous carbon is a pH-responsive supercapacitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a microporous polymer is converted into a micporous heterocarbon, and that the latter is an effective capacitive pH sensor.
a polymer of intrinsic micporosity is carbonized to a microporous carbon with retained nitrogen functionalities, which is then used to measure pH in aqueous solutions.

the microporosity in the heterocaron is the key factor for the high capacitance and the nitrogen functionalities provide a means to control and manipulate the electrochemical properties of the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carbonization of polymers containing nitrogen functionalities is a promising route for the synthesis of microporous carbons with unusual properties.
microporous carbons are not necessarily hydrophobic.
the carbonization of a nitrogen-containing PIM is a simple, direct route to a microporous, nitrogen-doped carbon material with unusual properties.
